questions.stem: Why does Aaron Falk return to Kiewarra at the start of the novel?
options: For the funeral of his childhood friend Luke Hadler and Luke's family
To investigate a fraud at the local school for the federal police
To sell the family farm he inherited when his father died
To give evidence at a new inquest into Ellie Deacon's death
questions.explanation: Luke, his wife Karen and their son Billy have been shot dead on their farm. Falk comes back for the funeral after a note from Luke's father, and is drawn into the case.

questions.stem: What does most of the town believe happened at the Hadler farm?
options: The family was shot by a neighbour in a dispute over water
Luke shot his wife and son, then turned the gun on himself
A stranger shot the family during a robbery at the farmhouse
Karen shot Luke and Billy, then turned the gun on herself
questions.explanation: Kiewarra assumes a murder-suicide by a farmer broken by the drought. The novel's main mystery is whether that easy explanation is true.

questions.stem: Who survives the killings at the Hadler farm?
options: Karen, who is found wounded in the house
Barb, Luke's mother, who was visiting
Charlotte, Luke and Karen's baby daughter
Billy, Luke and Karen's young son
questions.explanation: Baby Charlotte is found alive in the house. Why the killer left her becomes one of the puzzles of the case.

questions.stem: Why do Gerry and Barb Hadler ask Falk to stay on in Kiewarra?
options: They cannot believe Luke killed his family and want Falk to look into it
They want Falk to help them sell the farm before the bank takes it
They want Falk to look after Charlotte while they arrange the funeral
They believe Falk knows who killed Ellie Deacon and want him to confess
questions.explanation: Luke's parents ask Falk, a federal police officer, to look at the case again. Falk agrees reluctantly, partly out of guilt about the past.

questions.stem: Who works with Falk on the investigation?
options: Gretchen Schoner, who is now the senior detective in the district
Sergeant Greg Raco, the new local officer, who also doubts Luke's guilt
Mal Deacon, Ellie's father, who wants to clear the Hadler family name
Scott Whitlam, the school principal, who knew Karen through her work
questions.explanation: Raco has only just arrived in Kiewarra and has noticed details that do not fit a murder-suicide. As an outsider, he judges Falk on what he does, not on the town's gossip.

questions.stem: What happened to Ellie Deacon twenty years before the novel begins?
options: She was killed in a car crash after a party at the Hadler farm
She died in a bushfire that destroyed the Deacon family farm
She drowned in the river, and suspicion fell on the teenage Falk
She disappeared from the town, and her body was never found
questions.explanation: Ellie, one of Falk's close teenage friends, was found drowned. The town decided Falk was involved, and that suspicion still follows him.

questions.stem: Why did suspicion about Ellie's death fall on the Falks?
options: A note found in her room had the word 'Falk' and a date on it
Falk had been seen arguing with Ellie on the riverbank that day
Ellie's diary named Falk as the person she was afraid of
Falk's father had been seen driving Ellie out of the town
questions.explanation: The note could have meant Aaron or his father, Erik. Without anything more, the town turned against both of them.

questions.stem: What false alibi did Falk and Luke give for the day Ellie died?
options: That they had been working on the Hadler farm
That they had been at school until late that day
That they had been out shooting rabbits together
That they had been fishing together upstream
questions.explanation: Falk was really fishing alone, and Luke told him to say they had been shooting rabbits together. The lie protected Falk, but it also hid where Luke had been.

questions.stem: Why did Falk and his father leave Kiewarra twenty years earlier?
options: The drought ruined their farm and the bank took their land
Falk's father was charged over Ellie's death and lost his job
Threats from the town, led by Ellie's father, drove them out
Falk's father found a better-paid job on a farm in Queensland
questions.explanation: After Ellie's death, Mal Deacon and others made it clear the Falks were not welcome. They left for Melbourne, and Falk has stayed away ever since.

questions.stem: What does Falk find in one of Karen's library books?
options: A page torn from Ellie Deacon's diary, hidden for twenty years
A list of the farmers in the district who owed money to the bank
A receipt with the word 'Grant' and Falk's own phone number on it
A letter from Luke admitting that he had lied about Ellie's death
questions.explanation: The note seems to point to Grant Dow, Ellie's cousin. It shows that Karen had meant to contact Falk, which becomes the key to the case.

questions.stem: What did the word 'Grant' in Karen's note really refer to?
options: Grant Street in Clyde, where Karen planned to meet with Falk
A grant of money to the school, which the principal was stealing from
Grant Dow, whom Karen had seen near the farm on the day she died
A government drought grant that Luke had applied for and been refused
questions.explanation: Karen kept the school's books and found that money from a grant was missing. She wanted to tell Falk, who investigates financial crime. The name was a red herring that pointed readers at Grant Dow.

questions.stem: Who killed Luke, Karen and Billy Hadler?
options: Scott Whitlam, the principal of the local school
Grant Dow, Ellie Deacon's cousin and Falk's enemy
Jamie Sullivan, the last person to see Luke alive
Mal Deacon, Ellie's father, who hated the Hadlers
questions.explanation: Whitlam killed the family and made it look like a murder-suicide. The town's obvious suspects, including Grant Dow and Mal Deacon, were not involved.

questions.stem: Why did Scott Whitlam kill the Hadler family?
options: Karen had discovered he was the person who killed Ellie Deacon years earlier
Luke had refused to sell him the Hadler farm when the drought ruined him
Karen had found out he was stealing school grant money to pay his gambling debts
Luke had threatened to report him for selling stolen farm machinery in town
questions.explanation: Whitlam had taken grant money to pay gambling debts. When Karen raised the missing money with him, he killed her family to keep the theft hidden.

questions.stem: How did Whitlam reach the Hadler farm without his own car being seen?
options: He walked across the dry paddocks from the school, then hid in the shearing shed
He borrowed Jamie Sullivan's ute, so the cameras recorded the wrong vehicle
He arrived with Karen in her car, pretending to discuss the school's accounts
He rode a bike, stopped Luke on the road, then drove Luke's ute to the house
questions.explanation: Whitlam stopped Luke, killed him and drove Luke's ute to the farmhouse. The camera footage showed only Luke's ute arriving, which made Luke look guilty.

questions.stem: Why did Whitlam leave baby Charlotte alive?
options: She was too young to remember him or ever be a witness
He did not know she was in the house that afternoon
Karen had hidden her in a cupboard before he arrived
He was disturbed by Jamie Sullivan's car and fled
questions.explanation: Charlotte was too young to identify him, so she was no threat. Sparing her was self-interest, not mercy.

questions.stem: How does the final confrontation with Whitlam end?
options: He drowns in the river while trying to escape from a police search team
He sets fire to the dry bush, and Falk and Raco put it out, all three burned
He is shot by Raco as he tries to escape from the school in Luke's ute
He gives himself up at the pub after Falk explains the case to the town
questions.explanation: Cornered in the bush, Whitlam threatens to start a fire that could destroy the town. Falk and Raco smother the flames, and all three are badly burned but survive.

questions.stem: What does Falk find at the end of the novel?
options: Ellie's diary, in a childhood hiding place, revealing her father's abuse
Luke's confession, written the night before he was killed by Whitlam
The weapon used to kill Ellie, buried near the river where she drowned
A letter from his own father, explaining why they really left the town
questions.explanation: Before leaving, Falk goes back to a childhood hiding place and finds Ellie's diary. It shows that her father, Mal Deacon, had been abusing her.

questions.stem: What does the ending reveal about Ellie Deacon's death?
options: Whitlam killed her as a teenager, which is why he later feared Karen
Her father killed her when she planned to leave, and her cousin Grant knew
Luke pushed her into the river during an argument and then lied for years
She took her own life, and the note with Falk's name was a goodbye
questions.explanation: A final flashback shows that Mal Deacon killed Ellie when he learned she planned to leave, and Grant Dow was involved and kept the secret. Neither Falk nor Luke was responsible.

questions.stem: How does Harper show what happened on the day of the murders and in the past?
options: Through court transcripts from Whitlam's trial that open each part
Through flashback passages set apart from Falk's present-day investigation
Through Falk's police reports, printed in full at the end of each chapter
Through a first-person narrator who reveals everything in the final chapter
questions.explanation: Short flashbacks show the day of the killings and Falk's teenage years. They feed readers pieces of the truth, sometimes before Falk himself knows them.

questions.stem: What is Aaron Falk's job?
options: A lawyer in Melbourne who defends people accused of murder
A federal police officer who investigates financial crime
A homicide detective with the Victorian police in Geelong
A journalist in Sydney who writes about crime in country towns
questions.explanation: Falk works on money crimes, not murders. That is why Karen wanted to contact him about the missing grant money.

questions.stem: Why does Jamie Sullivan seem suspicious, and what is the truth?
options: He owed Luke money, but he had paid it back the week before the killings
He argued with Karen at the school, but only about Billy's schoolwork
He owned a shotgun like Luke's, but he had sold it months before
He lied about where he was, but he was secretly with the local doctor
questions.explanation: Jamie, the last person to see Luke alive, said he was at home with his grandmother. He was really with the local doctor, a secret he wanted to keep, and had nothing to do with the murders.

questions.stem: What role does Grant Dow play in the novel?
options: The publican, who tells Falk the truth about the principal's gambling
Luke's cousin, who was with him on the afternoon that Ellie died
Ellie's cousin, who looks guilty but did not kill the Hadlers
Ellie's brother, who blames Falk and led the town against the Falks
questions.explanation: Grant Dow bullies Falk and the note seems to name him, so he is an obvious suspect. He is innocent of the Hadler murders, but the ending ties him to Ellie's death.

questions.stem: Who is Gretchen Schoner?
options: A teenage friend who knows where Luke really was when Ellie died
The new school principal, who replaces Scott Whitlam after his arrest
Raco's wife, who helps Falk search the Hadler farm for missing evidence
Ellie's mother, who left Kiewarra years before her daughter drowned
questions.explanation: Falk, Luke, Ellie and Gretchen were close as teenagers. Gretchen eventually admits that Luke was with her that day, which explains part of the old lie.

questions.stem: How does the novel complicate Luke Hadler's character?
options: He is cleared of the murders, but is shown to be a liar who kept secrets
He is proved guilty of Ellie's death, though he did not kill his family
He turns out to have been Whitlam's partner in stealing the grant money
He is revealed as the person who drove the Falks out of the town
questions.explanation: Luke did not kill his family, but he lied about the day Ellie died and kept that lie going for twenty years. The novel shows that a victim can also be flawed.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Mal Deacon?
options: Ellie's grandfather, who suspected Luke for years but kept it to himself
Ellie's father, a violent bully who led the campaign against the Falks
Luke's father-in-law, who blames the drought for his daughter's death
The local policeman who first investigated Ellie Deacon's drowning
questions.explanation: Mal Deacon is openly hostile to Falk when he returns. The ending reveals him as the abuser, and the killer, of his own daughter.

questions.stem: Where is The Dry set?
options: Kiewarra, a fictional farming town in drought-stricken Victoria
Broken Hill, a real mining town in far western New South Wales
Melbourne, in the suburbs where Falk now lives and works
Alice Springs, a real town in the centre of Australia
questions.explanation: Kiewarra is invented, but it is drawn from real drought-hit farming towns. The heat, dust and failing farms press on every character.

questions.stem: Why do many people in Kiewarra find it easy to believe Luke killed his family?
options: Karen had told the police she was afraid of Luke the week before
The long drought has left farmers under severe financial strain
Luke had been charged with violent crimes several times before
Luke had told people at the pub that he planned to leave Karen
questions.explanation: With crops failing and debts rising, a farmer snapping under pressure seems believable. Harper uses that assumption to show how a community's fears shape what it sees.

questions.stem: The Dry is often described as 'rural noir'. Which feature fits the label?
options: A police team solving a crime with forensic science in a city laboratory
A cheerful amateur detective solving a puzzle in a quiet English village
A courtroom drama that follows a single trial from opening to verdict
A crime in an isolated country town, where the harsh landscape adds menace
questions.explanation: Rural noir moves the dark, morally complex crime story out of the city. In The Dry the drought, isolation and small-town secrets create the threat.

questions.stem: What do readers learn about Jane Harper's career before The Dry?
options: She was a teacher, and based Whitlam on a principal she had worked for
She was a journalist, and the novel won an award before it was published
She was a police officer, and drew on cases she had worked on in Victoria
She was a farmer, and wrote the novel during a drought on her own land
questions.explanation: Harper worked as a journalist, and The Dry won the Victorian Premier's Literary Award for an unpublished manuscript before it appeared in 2016.

questions.stem: How does the novel link its two mysteries?
options: Both were committed by the same killer, who returns to Kiewarra years later
Both are explained by the pressures of the drought on the farmers
Both expose old secrets, and Falk must face his past to solve the present
Both are solved by the same clue, a note found in Karen Hadler's library book
questions.explanation: The Hadler case reopens Ellie's death and the lie Falk and Luke told. Solving one forces Falk to confront the other.

questions.stem: How does the novel present the community of Kiewarra?
options: As close-knit, but quick to judge, gossip and turn on outsiders
As welcoming to Falk, who is treated as a local hero on his return
As divided between farmers and townspeople over water rights
As distrustful of police, so it closes ranks to protect Luke
questions.explanation: The town closed ranks against the Falks twenty years ago and quickly blamed Luke now. Harper shows how gossip and fear can stand in for the truth.

questions.stem: What does the drought come to symbolise in the novel?
options: The hope of renewal, since the rain arrives on the day the killer is caught
The farmers' resilience, as the whole town endures the hardship together as one
Nature's punishment of the town for the cover-up of Ellie's death
Pressure building in the town, so that tension and violence feel ready to ignite
questions.explanation: The heat and dry bush mirror the strain on the townspeople. The danger becomes literal at the climax, when Whitlam threatens to set the bush alight.

questions.stem: What does the novel suggest about guilt and the past?
options: Teenage mistakes are forgiven once the full truth comes out
Lies told to escape blame do not go away, and they shape lives for years
The past is best left alone, since digging it up only causes more harm
Guilt fades over time once people leave the town where the wrong was done
questions.explanation: Falk's alibi lie has followed him for twenty years and still links him to Ellie's death. Gretchen and Luke also carried guilt about that day.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of red herrings such as Jamie Sullivan's false alibi?
options: They lead readers toward wrong suspects, so the real solution surprises
They give readers the answer early, so the ending feels certain
They point readers straight to the real killer through carefully hidden clues
They build sympathy for suspects whom the town has wronged
questions.explanation: Jamie's lie, the 'Grant' note and Mal Deacon's hostility all point in the wrong direction. Each also reveals something about the town and its secrets.

questions.stem: From whose point of view is most of the present-day story told?
options: Gretchen's, so readers share her memories of Ellie
Whitlam's, so readers know the killer from the start
Falk's, so readers discover the clues as he does
Raco's, so readers see Falk through an outsider's eyes
questions.explanation: Following Falk keeps readers close to his reasoning and his doubts. It also means readers share his blind spots, which keeps the solution hidden.

questions.stem: The river where Ellie drowned has dried up in the drought. What is the effect?
options: It shows that the town has forgotten Ellie and moved on from her death
It marks the end of the farming way of life in Kiewarra for good
It explains why the Hadlers could not grow crops on their farm that year
It suggests the drought is exposing what the town has hidden
questions.explanation: The empty riverbed is a reminder of the old death at the heart of the town. Like the drought itself, it suggests secrets being laid bare.

questions.stem: Who sends Falk the note 'Luke lied. You lied. Be at the funeral.'?
options: Gerry Hadler, Luke's father
Mal Deacon, Ellie's father
Gretchen, Falk's old friend
Raco, the local sergeant
questions.explanation: Luke's father sends the note to make sure Falk comes back. It is the novel's first link between the Hadler deaths and the past.

questions.stem: What does Gerry's note 'Luke lied. You lied.' reveal?
options: Gerry believes that Luke and Falk planned the Hadler killings together
Gerry knows that Luke lied to Karen about the farm's money troubles
Gerry still suspects that Falk killed Ellie and wants him to confess at last
Gerry has always known that the boys' alibi for Ellie's death was false
questions.explanation: Gerry saw Luke riding his bike that afternoon, so he knew the rabbit-shooting story was untrue. The note shows that the town's past is not as settled as Falk hoped.

questions.stem: Which is the strongest topic sentence for the question 'Analyse how Harper uses the drought to shape the community of Kiewarra.'?
options: The Dry is set in a small town called Kiewarra, which is suffering through a long drought
This essay will discuss how the drought is shown in the novel The Dry by Jane Harper
Jane Harper published The Dry in 2016, and it was later made into a film with Eric Bana
Harper presents the drought as a pressure that turns the town's fear into suspicion and blame
questions.explanation: A strong topic sentence takes a position on the question and names what the paragraph will prove. The others retell, announce or state facts without making an argument.

questions.stem: A student writes: 'Lots of people in Kiewarra think Luke is guilty.' How could this be turned into analysis?
options: Retell the scene at the funeral in detail, in the order it happens
List the other suspects that Falk and Raco look at during the case
Explain how the town's quick judgement shows its readiness to blame
Add the names of all the people who believe that Luke is guilty
questions.explanation: Analysis explains what the evidence suggests. Linking the town's verdict on Luke to its treatment of the Falks connects the detail to the novel's ideas about judgement and blame.
